I lost my mom to cancer just before COVID, so I know what it feels like to watch someone you care about slip away. He lived the next state over, dropped everything, and is moving back here to be with her. It's been rough on him, and I wanted to do something special to take his mind off things, if only for a minute. This deal just fell in my lap. And it's even a genuine helmet, not one of those light replica Speedflex jobs. He is going to FREAK, and it's gonna be awesome. I have a whole rug pull planned. Gonna give him a cheap hat out of the leftover swag bin at work first, but in the inside I'm gonna leave a ticket redeemable with me for "one Packers Mystery Box item."

item.title: GovBrief Today #543
item.description: America chose sides. When the UN voted Friday to keep its human rights chief, 144 countries said yes. The United States and nine others, including Russia and North Korea, said no. France counted the votes out loud and posted that the world no longer listens to America. American diplomats answered Monday by walking out of a Security Council meeting on Russia's war while France spoke, and promising to do it again every time France speaks until the French take it back. Walkouts are a stunt as old as the UN itself, but the role was written for democracies snubbing pariahs, like France walking out on Russia's foreign minister after the invasion of Ukraine. America used the gesture on its oldest ally today and demanded an apology for being called out for voting against most of the world. item.title: Your Phone Isn't a Suitcase. It's Your Entire Fucking Life.
item.description: Encryption isn't suspicious. It's what responsible people do when they understand that the most valuable thing they own isn't the phone—it's everything inside it. The truly dangerous idea isn't that someone can protect their own data. It's that governments increasingly expect access first and justification later. A warrant used to be a constitutional safeguard. Now we're apparently being told it's an optional courtesy. When your phone contains your medical records, banking, private conversations, location history, photos, work documents, passwords, and the digital blueprint of your life, pretending it's no different than a piece of luggage is complete bullshit. Privacy isn't about having something to hide. It's about recognizing that freedom disappears the moment the state assumes your entire life should be available on demand. Today it's someone else's encrypted phone. Tomorrow it's your cloud storage. Next week it's your messages. Eventually it's the expectation that refusing access is itself evidence. Authoritarianism rarely arrives wearing jackboots. It arrives carrying paperwork and insisting it's all perfectly routine. If using strong security becomes probable cause, then the right to privacy has already been quietly hollowed out. The lock isn't the crime. Demanding every door remain unlocked is. #Privacy #Encryption #GrapheneOS #DigitalRights #FourthAmendment #CivilLiberties #CyberSecurity #Surveillance #Freedom #Technology #Imgur
